institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was looking for a quality university who offered economics courses for students which didn't neccesarily have a bachelor in Economics. Furthermore I wanted to live in a vibrant city - which one must say Paris is. So Sciences Po was a perfect choice. Very talented and ambitious students all located in one of the most interesting cities with a giant suply of cultural oppurtunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My experience has been great! In order to give it a 10 I would need the teaching at Sciences Po to be better. Obviously it might just be due to different teaching cultures in France and Denmark but I was dissapointed by some of my teachers preparedness level.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was difficult the first two weeks to figure out my oppurtunities to shift courses etc. But when I finally located the assistance team at their office they were very helpfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assistance with changing courses which suited my academic profile better.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was so lucky to find housing in Cite Universitaire. You had to write an application and was therafter chosen, so I will not describe it as particular easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I have enjoyed not to have all my everyday life to centrate on campus. More practically I would recommend living in the 11, 20 or 19 arrondissement. Super cool neighborhoods.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Sciences Po provided a short zoom-session where they told which steps to follow and what to prepare beforehand. The registration process itself was pretty intuitive at their website and I rembered it as they send quite a few emails with information and heads up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Zoom-session and e-mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was some of the courses that I had gotten pre-approved that I was not able to registrate for. After the first week however I got the oppurtunity to shift courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a prioritized list of which courses you would like to enroll for. Have a open mind in regards to courses you didnt initially wanted. One of my favourite courses was not even on my list.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
My fellow students was very talented, dilligent, nice and motivated. That fostered very insightfull conversations/discussion. I have definitely benefitted a lot from that. 

I think the teaching quality has been very varied. Some courses the professor was splendid others seemed to be way to busy doing other stuff than focusing on teaching. Also I don't necessarily think that the frequent testing and assignment writing fosters deep learning. You are simply to busy to dive deep into subjects. You have to finish your stuff quickly and move on to the next assignment.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As I stated earlier my fellow students has been very talented and the course readings has been interesting as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
At Sciences Po they put way more emphasis on active participation than at UCPH. That also means that students are talking a lot more than the professor. However I don't think the active participation format is well-suited for a class of 90 people... 

Furthermore there is more continuous testing and presentation at Sciences Po. That can feel overwhelming when you are not used to that. I had to get used to, that I couldnt hand in stuff with the same quality as back in Denmark. You simply do not have time for that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Math for Economist
- History of The Global Economy
- International Trade
- Developmental Economics
- History of Law & Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend Kevin H. O'Rourke's course "The History of the Global Economy". O'Rourke is a star and he convey the course material with such precision and nuance that you can't avoid being inspired and humbled.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries a more expensive than in Denmark. But you are in Paris so it is a good excuse to just eat out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All you can imagine. However there is limited spots for each activity.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I tried bouldering which is a nice way to get to know people. However it was mostly international students and not a lot of local Frenchmen - but I guess that is just how it is.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Buy a pass the jeune at SNCF and go with fast trains to other parts of France. Visit Fontaine-Bleau! You can take the train to Bois-le-Roi (there is a cute little local market on satursdays) and go for a hike or do some bouldering (it is a mekka).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People in Paris a very nice and welcoming and not much different from the Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Enroll in some sports-/cultural activities. Have courage! Say hello to the person next to you in the lecture room. That was how I met my best buddies down here.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Paris is a massive city and takes some time to get out the city. But go to all the lovely parks to rest you ears ;)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love going to concerts and Paris obviously offers a lot of oppurtunities for that. Download DICE and Shotgun, they gather music events. Otherwise I used Spotify a lot to discover concerts.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be aware that Sciences Po is a school for practioners. They are not very research oriented (at least not PSIA). That mean that they put emphasis on presentation and practical knowledge.

2. Make up with your self how much you wanna prioritize the studies and exploring Paris. There are assignment enough for you to do nothing else that studying if every single of them should be perfect...

3. Enroll in a french class. You won't talk much french if you dont attend a class. Despite the rumour Parisienne speaks perfectly English and they switch to English if they sense that you are not comfortable speaking French.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Practice your handwriting ;) You gonna need it for the 3-hour essay exams.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of things which has been rewarding. I have enjoyed just exploring Paris with completely new relations who comes from all-over the world. Realizing that you can establish new habits with new people has been empowering.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I've heard from a lot of people and now experienced my self that you will encounter a valley half-way threw. For me it was the end of October and I was drowning in midterm exams and I probably also missed my friend and familiy.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
